title: Beyond Policy Training: Recursive Solution Search from Unannotated Videos
claim: Planning backward from the goal yields a coarse roadmap that guides forward search, so only trials following it succeed.
layout: legend on top, 2 stacked panels, backward then forward, shared stage circles
description: A legend at the top defines dark and purple dots as states, a light-blue circle as a one-step forward reachable set R_-N, a red arrow as backward plan, a solid blue arrow as a correct forward trail, and a dashed purple arrow as an incorrect forward trail. Below are two gray panels. Panel 1, Backward Planning Stage, shows s_goal at the right with red arrows pointing left through shrinking-to-growing blue circles R_-1 to R_-4, ending at s_initial inside the largest circle. Panel 2, Forward Searching Stage, reuses the same circles. A solid blue path runs from s_initial through each circle to s_goal. Dashed purple arrows branch off at each stage toward purple dots outside the circles, marking failed trials. The eye goes first to the large blue circles and the contrast between the blue and purple arrows.
caption: Conceptual prototype for solution recovery from unannotated task executions. The prototype reasons recursively through a backward–forward process. First, backward planning starts from the goal and infers which intermediate stages must precede it, forming a coarse high-level roadmap. Second, forward search begins at the start state and follows this roadmap to guide environment interaction toward the goal. Correct trajectories remain aligned with the inferred roadmap, while incorrect trials deviate when their visited states no longer follow the inferred stage sequence.
abstract: Many real-world tasks are recorded as large collections of unannotated task executions, such as videos, which contain rich information about task progress but lack the supervision assumed by standard reinforcement learning (RL) pipelines. In many practical settings, the goal is not to train a reusable policy but simply to recover one feasible solution, making policy-centered learning unnecessarily costly. We propose Policy-Free Recursive Search (PFR-Search), a framework that directly recovers solutions from unannotated task executions without policy-grounded supervision or policy training. PFR-Search organizes videos into high-level task flows and performs recursive backward-forward search to recover solutions without policy modeling. To evaluate the efficiency of policy-free search in exploiting unannotated data, we use RL as an evaluation interface, incorporating task-flow-aligned intrinsic rewards and compare against video-driven RL methods. Experiments on long-horizon Minecraft tasks show that PFR-Search recovers feasible solutions from unannotated videos with minimal exploration.
